question.text:
Which of the following are common components of photochemical smog?
1. Chlorofluorocarbons
2. Acrolein
3. Ozone
4. Peroxyacetyl nitrate

solution.text:
The common components of photochemical smog are Ozone, Nitric oxide, Acrolein, Formaldehyde
and Peroxyacehyl nitrate (PAN).
Hence Chlorofluorocarbons (CFC) is not common component of photochemical smog.

question.text: Photochemical smog consists of excessive amount of X, in addition to aldehydes, ketones, peroxyacetyl nitrates (PAN) and so forth X is

solution.text:
Chemical pollutants in photochemical smog are nitrogen oxides (NO and NO2 ), volatile organic compounds, ozone O3 , peroxyacetyl nitrates.

In the presence of sunlight of the following reactions take place

NO2→hvNO+O

O+O2→O3

O3+NO→NO2+O2

Hence, it consists of excessive amount of ozone melecules.

question.text: Identify the pollutant gases largely responsible for the discoloured and lustreless nature of marble of the Taj Mahal.

solution.text:
Industries present nearby Taj Mahal produce a lot of NO2 and SO2 gases which react with water, oxygen and other chemicals to form sulphuric acid and nitric acid. These then mix with water and make the rain acidic which than react with marble to decolourise it as follows
CaCO3+H2SO4→CaSO4+CO2+H2O

options.text: Its concentration increases with temperature increase of atmosphere.
It is used as an insecticide which is air pollutant

It reacts with <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mtext>O</mtext>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  </mrow></math> and <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mtext>H</mtext>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  <mtext>O</mtext></mrow></math> to produce acid rain

solution.text: <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mrow>    <mtext>SO</mtext></mrow>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  </mrow></math> is considered as air pollutant because it reacts with <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mtext>O</mtext>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  </mrow></math> and <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mtext>H</mtext>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  <mtext>O</mtext></mrow></math> to produce acid rain. Oxides from nitrogen and sulphur, released into the atmosphere from thermal power plants, industries and automobiles are the main sources of acid rain. These oxides on oxidation followed by hydrolysis give sulphuric acid and nitric acid that get dissolved in rain water and are responsible for the acidity of rain.

question.text: A petroleum fraction having boiling range 70− 200 o  C and containing 6−10 carbon atoms per molecule is called

solution.text:
The bulk of a typical gasoline consists of hydrocarbons with between 4 and 12 carbon atoms per molecule (commonly referred to as C4−C12). It is a mixture of paraffins (alkanes), cycloalkanes (naphthenes), and olefins (alkenes), where the usage of the terms paraffin and olefin is particular to the oil industry. The actual ratio depends on:

  • The oil refinery that makes the gasoline, as not all refineries have the same set of processing units;
  • The crude oil feed used by the refinery;
  • The grade of gasoline, in particular, the octane rating.

Below carbon atoms per molecule are mentioned.

(i) Gasoline C6-C10

(ii) Kerosene C10-C13

(iii) Gas oil C13-C18
